scenes.script: The worst quarter in years. Then, the best since twenty-twenty. Same market — ninety days apart.
scenes.headline:
90 DAYS.
TOTAL
WHIPLASH.

scenes.script: Q1 was the storm. The Iran conflict sent oil from sixty-one dollars to one-eighteen — up ninety-four percent. The S&P fell four point three. The Nasdaq dropped seven.
scenes.label: Q1 · JAN–MAR · THE STORM
scenes.headline:
FIRST,
THE STORM.

scenes.script: But here's what most people missed: the crash was narrow. Two hundred and ninety of the five hundred stocks actually beat the index. Equal-weighted? Up zero point seven.
scenes.label: Q1 · UNDER THE HOOD
scenes.headline:
THE CRASH
WAS NARROW.

scenes.script: Then came the flip. Q2: the S&P surged fourteen point nine percent — the best quarter since twenty-twenty. The Dow closed at a record.
scenes.label: Q2 · APR–JUN · THE COMEBACK
scenes.headline:
BEST QUARTER
SINCE 2020.

big.caption: S&P 500 · Q2 2026 — Dow at a record

scenes.script: And the fuel wasn't hype. Profit forecasts jumped from eighteen point eight percent, to twenty-three point one. Earnings did the lifting.
scenes.label: Q2 · THE FUEL
scenes.headline:
EARNINGS
DID IT.

scenes.script: Now, the warning light. Inflation: two point four in January. Four point two by May. The thirty-year Treasury touched five percent. Bonds are not celebrating.
scenes.label: THE WARNING LIGHT
scenes.headline:
BONDS AREN'T
BUYING IT.

scenes.script: And one more crack: hiring. May added one hundred and seventy-two thousand jobs. June? Just fifty-seven — half the forecast. The labor market is cooling, fast.
scenes.label: THE OTHER CRACK
scenes.headline:
HIRING IS
STALLING.

scenes.script: Neither is Bitcoin having fun. Thirteen straight days of ETF outflows. Sixty-seven six, down to sixty thousand — a twenty-one month low. Two red quarters in a row.
scenes.label: THE ODD ONE OUT
scenes.headline:
BITCOIN
MISSED IT.

scenes.script: So: stocks at records. Inflation rising. Jobs cooling. Bitcoin sinking. Pick your signal.
scenes.headline:
PICK YOUR
SIGNAL.

scenes.script: Next quarter: bank earnings open in mid-July. Warsh delivers his first official forecasts in September. And every single inflation print decides the rate path. Follow for the briefings — and see you in Q3.
scenes.headline:
SEE YOU
IN Q3.
